explain.say: A canal lock's gates are not flat doors. Each pair is made of two leaves that meet at an angle, forming a V that points toward the higher water. These are called mitre gates.

faq.q: Why do lock gates make a V shape?
faq.a: The V, pointing upstream, lets water pressure push the two leaves together so they wedge shut, like an arch on its side. The higher the water, the tighter the seal.

faq.q: How strong is the water push on a lock gate?
faq.a: Very strong. Pressure grows with depth, so a gate holding back a few metres of water feels a total push of many tonnes. That is why gates are built of thick oak or steel.
asks: How much force is on a lock gate?

faq.q: What are paddles in a lock?
faq.a: Paddles are small sluice gates, in the lock gates or in tunnels in the walls, that let water flow in or out to fill or empty the lock before the main gates are opened.
asks: How does a lock fill with water?

faq.q: Why can't you open lock gates until the water is level?
faq.a: While one side is higher, water pressure pins the gates shut with a force of many tonnes. Once the levels match, the forces balance and the gates swing open with a steady push.
asks: Why won't the lock gate open?

faq.a: Mitre gates are often credited to Leonardo da Vinci, who worked on canal locks in Milan in the late 1400s. They are still the standard design today.
asks: Did Leonardo da Vinci invent lock gates?

facts: Mitre lock gates, often credited to Leonardo da Vinci in the late 1400s, are still the most common lock gate design.
Water pressure on a lock gate rises with depth, so the bottom of the gate takes the greatest push.
